## midiwire

*   **See**: [https://github.com/alexferl/midiwire][295] for full documentation
*   **See**: [https://github.com/alexferl/midiwire#quick-start][296] for quick start guide

midiwire - Browser-based MIDI controller framework

A lightweight, zero-dependency library for creating web-based MIDI controllers.
Features declarative HTML binding via data attributes, programmatic APIs,
bidirectional MIDI communication, SysEx support, voice management, and more.

Works with the Web MIDI API in Chrome, Firefox, and Opera. Provides multiple
integration approaches from fully declarative (HTML-only) to fully programmatic (JavaScript-only).

## Features

*   Declarative binding via data attributes (zero JavaScript)
*   Programmatic binding with full control
*   Bidirectional MIDI communication (send/receive)
*   SysEx support
*   Patch management (save/load presets)
*   Hotplug device detection
*   Comprehensive event system
*   DX7 voice/parameter management

### Examples

```javascript
// Quick start - Auto-binding with data attributes
import { createMIDIController } from 'midiwire';

const midi = await createMIDIController({
  channel: 1,
  selector: '[data-midi-cc]',
  watchDOM: true
});

// In your HTML:
// <input type="range" min="0" max="127" data-midi-cc="74" data-midi-label="Filter">
// <input type="range" min="0" max="127" data-midi-cc="7" data-midi-label="Volume">
```

```javascript
// Programmatic binding
import { MIDIController } from 'midiwire';

const midi = new MIDIController({ channel: 1 });
await midi.init();
await midi.connect('My Synth');

const cutoff = document.getElementById('cutoff');
midi.bind(cutoff, { cc: 74 });
```

```javascript
// Device manager with UI integration
import { createMIDIDeviceManager } from 'midiwire';

const deviceManager = await createMIDIDeviceManager({
  onStatusUpdate: (message, state) => {
    document.getElementById('status').textContent = message;
  }
});

// Populate device dropdown
const select = document.getElementById('device-select');
deviceManager.populateDeviceList(select);
deviceManager.connectDeviceSelection(select);
```

## MIDIControlsOptions

Options for createMIDIController()

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `selector` **[string][298]?** CSS selector for auto-binding elements that have data-midi-\* attributes
*   `channel` **[number][299]?** Default MIDI channel (1-16)
*   `output` **([string][298] | [number][299])?** MIDI output device name, ID, or index to auto-connect to
*   `sysex` **[boolean][300]?** Request SysEx access for sending/receiving system exclusive messages
*   `autoConnect` **[boolean][300]?** Auto-connect to first available output device
*   `watchDOM` **[boolean][300]?** Automatically bind dynamically added elements using MutationObserver
*   `onReady` **[Function][301]?** Callback when MIDI is ready, receives (controller) as parameter
*   `onError` **[Function][301]?** Error handler for MIDI access errors
*   `input` **([string][298] | [number][299])?** MIDI input device name, ID, or index to connect to for receiving MIDI

### Examples

```javascript
// Basic auto-binding
const options = {
  selector: '[data-midi-cc]',
  channel: 1,
  watchDOM: true
};
```

```javascript
// Connect to specific device
const options = {
  output: 'My MIDI Keyboard',
  channel: 2,
  sysex: true
};
```

## createMIDIController

Create and initialize a MIDI controller with optional auto-binding. This factory function
creates a MIDIController instance, initializes it, and optionally sets up declarative binding
using DataAttributeBinder. Perfect for getting started quickly or when using data attributes.

### Parameters

*   `options` **[MIDIControlsOptions][4]** Configuration options (optional, default `{}`)

### Examples

```javascript
// Quick start with auto-binding
const midi = await createMIDIController({
  selector: '[data-midi-cc]',
  watchDOM: true
});
```

```javascript
// Auto-bind with specific device and channel
const midi = await createMIDIController({
  output: 'My Synth',
  channel: 2,
  selector: '[data-midi-cc]',
  onReady: (controller) => {
    console.log('MIDI ready!');
  }
});
```

```javascript
// Programmatic binding (no auto-bind)
const midi = await createMIDIController({
  autoConnect: false,
  channel: 1
});
await midi.connectOutput('My Synth');
const slider = document.getElementById('cutoff');
midi.bind(slider, { cc: 74 });
```

```javascript
// With SysEx support
const midi = await createMIDIController({
  sysex: true,
  onReady: (controller) => {
    // Send SysEx after connection
    controller.sendSysEx([0x41, 0x10, 0x42]);
  }
});
```

*   Throws **[MIDIAccessError][147]** If MIDI access is denied or browser doesn't support Web MIDI API

Returns **[Promise][302]<[MIDIController][37]>** A promise resolving to the initialized MIDIController instance

## MIDIDeviceManagerOptions

Options for createMIDIDeviceManager()

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `onStatusUpdate` **[Function][301]?** Callback for status updates (message: string, state: string)
*   `onConnectionUpdate` **[Function][301]?** Callback when connection status changes (device: Object, midi: MIDIController)
*   `channel` **[number][299]?** Default MIDI channel (1-16)
*   `output` **([string][298] | [number][299])?** MIDI output device name, ID, or index to auto-connect to
*   `sysex` **[boolean][300]?** Request SysEx access
*   `onReady` **[Function][301]?** Callback when MIDI is ready, receives (midi: MIDIController, deviceManager: MIDIDeviceManager)
*   `onError` **[Function][301]?** Error handler for MIDI access errors
*   `selector` **[string][298]?** CSS selector for auto-binding controls
*   `watchDOM` **[boolean][300]?** Automatically bind dynamically added elements
*   `input` **([string][298] | [number][299])?** MIDI input device name, ID, or index to connect to

### Examples

```javascript
// Basic device manager setup
const options = {
  channel: 1,
  onStatusUpdate: (message, state) => updateStatusUI(message, state)
};
```

```javascript
// Full device manager with UI integration
const options = {
  output: 'My Synth',
  channel: 2,
  sysex: true,
  selector: '[data-midi-cc]',
  watchDOM: true,
  onStatusUpdate: (message, state) => {
    console.log(message);
    document.getElementById('status').textContent = message;
  },
  onReady: (midi, deviceManager) => {
    // Populate device dropdown
    const select = document.getElementById('device-select');
    deviceManager.populateDeviceList(select);
    deviceManager.connectDeviceSelection(select);
  }
};
```

## createMIDIDeviceManager

Create a MIDIDeviceManager with an integrated MIDIController. This factory function creates a complete
device management solution including MIDIController, auto-binding (optional), and device manager UI helpers.
Perfect for applications that need device selection UI and status management.

### Parameters

*   `options` **[MIDIDeviceManagerOptions][10]** Configuration options (optional, default `{}`)

### Examples

```javascript
// Basic device manager
const deviceManager = await createMIDIDeviceManager({
  channel: 1,
  onStatusUpdate: (message, state) => {
    console.log(message);
  }
});

// Access the MIDIController via deviceManager.midi
const midi = deviceManager.midi;
midi.bind(document.getElementById('cutoff'), { cc: 74 });
```

```javascript
// With auto-connect and status UI
const deviceManager = await createMIDIDeviceManager({
  output: 'My Synth',
  channel: 2,
  selector: '[data-midi-cc]',
  onStatusUpdate: (message, state) => {
    const statusEl = document.getElementById('status');
    statusEl.textContent = message;
    statusEl.className = state;
  }
});
```

```javascript
// Complete UI integration with device dropdown
const deviceManager = await createMIDIDeviceManager({
  channel: 1,
  sysex: true,
  onStatusUpdate: (message, state) => {
    document.getElementById('status').textContent = message;
  },
  onReady: async (midi, dm) => {
    // Setup device selection
    const deviceSelect = document.getElementById('device-select');
    dm.populateDeviceList(deviceSelect);
    dm.connectDeviceSelection(deviceSelect);

    // Setup channel selection
    const channelSelect = document.getElementById('channel-select');
    dm.connectChannelSelection(channelSelect);
  }
});
```

*   Throws **[MIDIAccessError][147]** If MIDI access is denied or browser doesn't support Web MIDI API

Returns **[Promise][302]<[MIDIDeviceManager][109]>** A promise resolving to the initialized MIDIDeviceManager instance

## DataAttributeBinder

Declarative MIDI binding system using HTML data attributes. Enables zero-JavaScript
MIDI controller creation by scanning the DOM for data-midi-\* attributes and automatically
binding elements to MIDIController.

Features:

*   **Auto-discovery**: Scans DOM for data-midi-\* attributes
*   **7-bit CC**: Bind with `data-midi-cc="74"` (e.g., Filter Cutoff)
*   **14-bit CC**: Bind with `data-midi-msb="74" data-midi-lsb="75"` for high resolution
*   **Custom ranges**: Use HTML min/max attributes or `data-midi-min`/`data-midi-max`
*   **Channel override**: `data-midi-channel="2"` to use channel 2 instead of default
*   **Value inversion**: `data-midi-invert="true"` to invert the value mapping
*   **De bouncing**: `data-midi-debounce="100"` for high-frequency updates (ms)
*   **Auto-binding**: Watch DOM for dynamically added/removed elements with MutationObserver
*   **Labeling**: `data-midi-label="Filter Cutoff"` for patch saving

### Parameters

*   `controller` &#x20;
*   `selector` **[string][298]** CSS selector for elements to bind. Defaults to looking for data-midi-cc or data-midi-msb/lmb attributes (optional, default `"[data-midi-cc]"`)

### Examples

```javascript
// 7-bit CC binding
<input type="range" min="0" max="127" data-midi-cc="74" data-midi-label="Filter Cutoff">
```

```javascript
// 14-bit high-resolution binding
<input type="range" min="0" max="16383" data-midi-msb="74" data-midi-lsb="75" data-midi-label="Pitch Bend">
```

```javascript
// With channel override and inversion
<input type="range" min="0" max="127" data-midi-cc="7" data-midi-channel="2" data-midi-invert="true" data-midi-label="Volume">
```

```javascript
// With custom range
<input type="range" min="-100" max="100" data-midi-cc="10" data-midi-label="Pan">
```

```javascript
// Complete setup with auto-binding
const midi = new MIDIController();
const binder = new DataAttributeBinder(midi);

// Bind existing elements
binder.bindAll();

// Enable auto-binding for dynamically added elements
binder.enableAutoBinding();
```

```javascript
// Manual binding with custom selector
const binder = new DataAttributeBinder(midi, '[data-midi-cc]');
binder.bindAll();
```

### bindAll

Bind all matching elements in the document to MIDI Controller. Searches the DOM for elements
that match the selector and have data-midi-\* attributes. Skips already bound elements (marked
with data-midi-bound attribute). Automatically handles both 7-bit CC and 14-bit CC configurations.

#### Examples

```javascript
// Bind all elements with data-midi-cc or data-midi-msb/lmb attributes
binder.bindAll();
```

```javascript
// Bind after DOM is loaded
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
  binder.bindAll();
});
```

```javascript
// Bind after MIDI is ready
midi.on(midi.READY, () => {
  binder.bindAll();
});
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

### enableAutoBinding

Enable automatic binding of dynamically added elements using MutationObserver.
Watches the DOM for new elements that match the selector and have data-midi-\* attributes,
automatically binding them when they're added. Also handles cleanup of removed elements.

#### Examples

```javascript
// Enable and forget - perfect for single page apps
binder.enableAutoBinding();
```

```javascript
// Add controls dynamically
binder.enableAutoBinding();
// Later, when you add new UI controls:
const newSlider = document.createElement('input');
newSlider.type = 'range';
newSlider.setAttribute('data-midi-cc', '71');
document.getElementById('controls').appendChild(newSlider);
// Automatically bound! ✨
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

### disableAutoBinding

Disable automatic binding and clean up the MutationObserver. Stops watching for
dynamically added/removed elements and disconnects the observer to prevent memory leaks.

#### Examples

```javascript
// Temporarily disable auto-binding
binder.disableAutoBinding();
// Make bulk DOM changes
updateAllControls();
// Re-enable when done
binder.enableAutoBinding();
```

```javascript
// Clean up when done with the binder
binder.disableAutoBinding();
binder.destroy();
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

### destroy

Clean up resources and disconnect any active observers. Disables auto-binding if active
and disconnects the MutationObserver to prevent memory leaks. Call this when done with
the binder instance.

#### Examples

```javascript
// Clean up when done
const binder = new DataAttributeBinder(midi);
binder.bindAll();
binder.enableAutoBinding();

// Later, when cleaning up
binder.destroy();
```

```javascript
// Clean up in response to user action
document.getElementById('cleanup-btn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  binder.destroy();
});
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

## PatchData

Complete patch data structure for saving/loading controller state

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `name` **[string][298]** Patch/preset name
*   `device` **([string][298] | null)** Output device name (if saved with device)
*   `timestamp` **[string][298]** ISO timestamp when patch was created
*   `version` **[string][298]** Patch format version (e.g., "1.0")
*   `channels` **[Object][297]<[number][299], [ChannelData][30]>** Channel data indexed by channel number (1-16)
*   `settings` **[Object][297]<[string][298], [SettingData][32]>** Control settings indexed by control key

### Examples

```javascript
const patch = {
  name: "My Synth Patch",
  device: "My MIDI Keyboard",
  timestamp: "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z",
  version: "1.0",
  channels: {
    1: {
      ccs: { 7: 100, 74: 64 },
      program: 5,
      pitchBend: 8192
    }
  },
  settings: {
    cc7: { min: 0, max: 127, invert: false, is14Bit: false, label: "Volume" }
  }
};
```

## ChannelData

Channel-specific MIDI data

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `ccs` **[Object][297]<[number][299], [number][299]>** Control Change values indexed by CC number (0-127)
*   `notes` **[Object][297]<[number][299], [number][299]>** Note on/off states indexed by note number (0-127)
*   `program` **[number][299]?** Program change value for the channel (0-127)
*   `pitchBend` **[number][299]?** Pitch bend value for the channel (0-16383, center=8192)
*   `monoPressure` **[number][299]?** Channel pressure/aftertouch value (0-127)
*   `polyPressure` **[Object][297]<[number][299], [number][299]>?** Polyphonic pressure values indexed by note number

## SettingData

Control binding settings

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `min` **[number][299]** Minimum input value
*   `max` **[number][299]** Maximum input value
*   `invert` **[boolean][300]** Whether to invert the value mapping
*   `is14Bit` **[boolean][300]** Whether this is a 14-bit CC control
*   `label` **([string][298] | null)** Optional display label
*   `elementId` **([string][298] | null)** Associated DOM element ID
*   `onInput` **([Function][301] | null)** Optional callback for value updates

## CONTROLLER\_EVENTS

Controller event constants. Events are organized by category and follow a consistent naming pattern:

*   Core events (READY, ERROR, DESTROYED)
*   Device events (DEV\_\*)
*   Channel events (CH\_\*)
*   System events (SYS\_\*)
*   Patch events (PATCH\_\*)

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `READY` **[string][298]** Emitted when controller is initialized and ready
*   `ERROR` **[string][298]** Emitted on errors
*   `DESTROYED` **[string][298]** Emitted when controller is destroyed
*   `DEV_OUT_CONNECTED` **[string][298]** Emitted when output device is connected
*   `DEV_IN_CONNECTED` **[string][298]** Emitted when input device is connected
*   `CH_CC_SEND` **[string][298]** Emitted when sending control change
*   `CH_CC_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving control change
*   `CH_NOTE_ON_SEND` **[string][298]** Emitted when sending note on
*   `CH_NOTE_ON_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving note on
*   `CH_NOTE_OFF_SEND` **[string][298]** Emitted when sending note off
*   `CH_NOTE_OFF_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving note off
*   `CH_PC_SEND` **[string][298]** Emitted when sending program change
*   `CH_PC_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving program change
*   `CH_PITCH_BEND_SEND` **[string][298]** Emitted when sending pitch bend
*   `CH_PITCH_BEND_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving pitch bend
*   `CH_MONO_PRESS_SEND` **[string][298]** Emitted when sending channel pressure
*   `CH_MONO_PRESS_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving channel pressure
*   `CH_POLY_PRESS_SEND` **[string][298]** Emitted when sending polyphonic pressure
*   `CH_POLY_PRESS_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving polyphonic pressure
*   `SYS_EX_SEND` **[string][298]** Emitted when sending SysEx
*   `SYS_EX_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving SysEx
*   `SYS_CLOCK_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving MIDI clock
*   `SYS_START_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving start command
*   `SYS_CONTINUE_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving continue command
*   `SYS_STOP_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving stop command
*   `SYS_MTC_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving MTC
*   `SYS_SONG_POS_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving song position
*   `SYS_SONG_SEL_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving song selection
*   `SYS_TUNE_REQ_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving tune request
*   `SYS_ACT_SENSE_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving active sensing
*   `SYS_RESET_RECV` **[string][298]** Emitted when receiving system reset
*   `MIDI_RAW` **[string][298]** Emitted for unhandled raw MIDI messages
*   `PATCH_SAVED` **[string][298]** Emitted when a patch is saved
*   `PATCH_LOADED` **[string][298]** Emitted when a patch is loaded
*   `PATCH_DELETED` **[string][298]** Emitted when a patch is deleted

### Examples

```javascript
// Listen for controller ready
midi.on(midi.READY, (controller) => {
  console.log('MIDI ready!');
});
```

```javascript
// Listen for CC messages (both send and receive)
midi.on(midi.CH_CC_SEND, ({ cc, value, channel }) => {
  console.log(`Sent CC ${cc}: ${value} on channel ${channel}`);
});

midi.on(midi.CH_CC_RECV, ({ cc, value, channel }) => {
  console.log(`Received CC ${cc}: ${value} on channel ${channel}`);
});
```

```javascript
// Listen for device connections
midi.on(midi.DEV_OUT_CONNECTED, (device) => {
  console.log(`Output connected: ${device.name}`);
});
```

## MIDIController

**Extends EventEmitter**

Main controller for browser-based MIDI operations. Provides APIs for:

*   Device management (connect/disconnect, enumerate devices)
*   Control binding (DOM elements <-> MIDI CC)
*   MIDI messaging (send/receive CC, Note, SysEx)
*   Patch management (save/load presets)
*   Event handling (MIDI messages, connection changes, errors)

### Parameters

*   `options` **[Object][297]**  (optional, default `{}`)

### Examples

```javascript
// Basic initialization
const midi = new MIDIController({ channel: 1 });
await midi.init();
```

```javascript
// Bind UI controls to MIDI CCs
const volumeSlider = document.getElementById('volume');
midi.bind(volumeSlider, { cc: 7 }); // Bind CC 7 (volume)
```

```javascript
// Send MIDI messages
midi.channel.sendCC(74, 64); // Send CC 74 (filter cutoff) value 64
midi.channel.sendNoteOn(60, 100); // Play middle C with velocity 100
midi.channel.sendNoteOff(60); // Stop middle C
```

```javascript
// Listen for MIDI events
midi.on(midi.CH_CC_RECV, ({ cc, value, channel }) => {
  console.log(`CC ${cc} received: ${value}`);
});
```

```javascript
// Save and load patches
const patch = midi.patch.get('My Patch');
midi.patch.save('My Patch');
midi.patch.load('My Patch');
```

### init

Initialize MIDI access. Requests browser permission and connects to devices.
Emits 'ready' event on success, 'error' event on failure.

#### Examples

```javascript
// Basic initialization
const midi = new MIDIController();
await midi.init();
```

```javascript
// Initialization with custom options
const midi = new MIDIController({
  channel: 2,
  sysex: true,
  autoConnect: false
});
await midi.init();
```

```javascript
// With event listeners
const midi = new MIDIController();
midi.on(midi.READY, (controller) => {
  console.log('MIDI ready!');
});
midi.on(midi.ERROR, (error) => {
  console.error('MIDI error:', error);
});
await midi.init();
```

*   Throws **[MIDIAccessError][147]** If MIDI access is denied or browser doesn't support Web MIDI

Returns **[Promise][302]\<void>**&#x20;

### bind

Bind a DOM element to a MIDI CC for bidirectional control. Automatically handles
value normalization based on element type (slider, knob, etc.) and MIDI range (0-127).
Sends initial MIDI value when binding if controller is initialized.

#### Parameters

*   `element` **[HTMLElement][303]** DOM element to bind (e.g., input range, number input)
*   `config` **[Object][297]** Binding configuration

    *   `config.cc` **[number][299]** CC number (0-127, e.g., 7 for volume, 74 for filter cutoff)
    *   `config.min` **[number][299]** Minimum input value (auto-detected from element if available) (optional, default `0`)
    *   `config.max` **[number][299]** Maximum input value (auto-detected from element if available) (optional, default `127`)
    *   `config.channel` **[number][299]?** MIDI channel (defaults to controller's default channel)
    *   `config.invert` **[boolean][300]** Invert the value mapping (optional, default `false`)
    *   `config.is14Bit` **[boolean][300]** Use 14-bit CC (MSB + LSB, requires msb/lsb config) (optional, default `false`)
    *   `config.msb` **[number][299]?** MSB CC number for 14-bit control
    *   `config.lsb` **[number][299]?** LSB CC number for 14-bit control
    *   `config.onInput` **[Function][301]?** Optional callback for value updates (receives normalized element value)
*   `options` **[Object][297]** Additional options (optional, default `{}`)

    *   `options.debounce` **[number][299]** Debounce delay in ms for high-frequency updates (optional, default `0`)

#### Examples

```javascript
// Basic slider binding
const volumeSlider = document.getElementById('volume');
const unbindVolume = midi.bind(volumeSlider, { cc: 7 }); // CC 7 = Channel Volume
```

```javascript
// Binding with custom range and inversion
const filterKnob = document.getElementById('filter');
midi.bind(filterKnob, {
  cc: 74,        // CC 74 = Filter Cutoff
  min: 0,        // Knob minimum value
  max: 127,      // Knob maximum value
  invert: true   // Invert value (useful for cutoff - higher CC = brighter)
});
```

```javascript
// 14-bit high-resolution control
const fineTune = document.getElementById('fine-tune');
midi.bind(fineTune, {
  is14Bit: true,
  msb: 0,    // CC 0 = MSB
  lsb: 32    // CC 32 = LSB
});
```

```javascript
// With debouncing for high-frequency updates
const lfoRate = document.getElementById('lfo-rate');
midi.bind(lfoRate, { cc: 76 }, { debounce: 50 }); // 50ms debounce
```

```javascript
// Using callback to update display
const pitchSlider = document.getElementById('pitch');
const pitchDisplay = document.getElementById('pitch-value');
midi.bind(pitchSlider, {
  cc: 75,
  onInput: (value) => {
    pitchDisplay.textContent = Math.round(value);
  }
});
```

Returns **[Function][301]** Unbind function - Call to remove binding and cleanup event listeners

### unbind

Unbind a control

#### Parameters

*   `element` **[HTMLElement][303]**&#x20;

### destroy

Clean up resources

Connect to a MIDI output device

Returns **[Promise][302]\<void>**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][302]\<void>**&#x20;

## MIDIDeviceManager

High-level MIDI device manager for web UIs. Provides simplified APIs for:

*   Populating device select dropdowns with available MIDI outputs
*   Handling device connections/disconnections with status updates
*   Tracking connection state and current device
*   Updating UI elements on device changes
*   Managing MIDI channel selection

NOTE: Typically used with createMIDIDeviceManager() factory function.
For direct MIDI I/O and control binding, use MIDIController instead.

### Parameters

*   `options` **[Object][297]** Configuration options (optional, default `{}`)

### Examples

```javascript
// Basic usage with MIDIController
const midi = new MIDIController();
await midi.init();

const manager = new MIDIDeviceManager({ midiController: midi });
const deviceSelect = document.getElementById('device-select');
const channelSelect = document.getElementById('channel-select');

// Set up device list dropdown
manager.populateDeviceList(deviceSelect);

// Handle device selection
manager.connectDeviceSelection(deviceSelect, (midi, device) => {
  console.log(`Connected to ${device.name}`);
});

// Handle channel selection
manager.connectChannelSelection(channelSelect);
```

```javascript
// With status and connection callbacks
const manager = new MIDIDeviceManager({
  midiController: midi,
  onStatusUpdate: (message, state) => {
    console.log(`Status: ${message}`);
    document.getElementById('status').textContent = message;
  },
  onConnectionUpdate: (device, midi) => {
    console.log('Connection state changed');
  }
});
```

### setMIDI

Initialize the device manager with a MIDIController

#### Parameters

*   `midi` **[MIDIController][37]**&#x20;

### setupDeviceListeners

Set up device change event listeners for automatic UI updates when devices
connect or disconnect. Handles both successful connections and disconnections,
updating status messages and tracking the current device state.

#### Parameters

*   `onDeviceListChange` **[Function][301]?** Optional callback to refresh device list UI when devices change

#### Examples

```javascript
// Basic setup
manager.setupDeviceListeners();
```

```javascript
// With device list refresh callback
manager.setupDeviceListeners(() => {
  manager.populateDeviceList(deviceSelect);
});
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

### updateStatus

Update status message and trigger status callback

#### Parameters

*   `message` **[string][298]** Status message to display
*   `state` **[string][298]** Status state (e.g., 'connected', 'error', 'warning') (optional, default `''`)

#### Examples

```javascript
manager.updateStatus('Connected to MIDI keyboard', 'connected');
```

```javascript
manager.updateStatus('Connection failed', 'error');
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

### updateConnectionStatus

Update connection status

### getOutputDevices

Get the current list of MIDI output devices

Returns **[Array][304]<[Object][297]>** Array of device objects with id, name, manufacturer

### getInputDevices

Get the current list of MIDI input devices

Returns **[Array][304]<[Object][297]>** Array of device objects with id, name, manufacturer

### isDeviceConnected

Check if a device is still connected

#### Parameters

*   `deviceName` **[string][298]**&#x20;

Returns **[boolean][300]**&#x20;

### connectDeviceSelection

Connect device selection events to automatically handle device connections when
the user selects a device from a dropdown. Handles both connection and disconnection.
Also manages connection state to prevent concurrent connection attempts.

#### Parameters

*   `deviceSelectElement` **[HTMLSelectElement][306]** The select element populated with devices
*   `onConnect` **[Function][301]** Callback when device is successfully connected (midi: MIDIController, device: Object)

#### Examples

```javascript
// Basic device selection
const deviceSelect = document.getElementById('device-select');
manager.connectDeviceSelection(deviceSelect, (midi, device) => {
  console.log(`Connected to ${device.name}`);
});
```

```javascript
// With setup complete callback
manager.connectDeviceSelection(deviceSelect, async (midi, device) => {
  // Send initial program change after connection
  midi.channel.sendPC(5);
  // Load saved patch for this device
  await loadDevicePatch(device.name);
});
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

### connectChannelSelection

Connect channel selection events to automatically update the MIDI channel when
the user selects a different channel from a dropdown. Triggers connection status
update to notify listeners of the channel change.

#### Parameters

*   `channelSelectElement` **[HTMLSelectElement][306]** The select element with channel options (1-16)

#### Examples

```javascript
// Setup channel selection
const channelSelect = document.getElementById('channel-select');
manager.connectChannelSelection(channelSelect);
```

```javascript
// Combined with device selection
manager.connectDeviceSelection(deviceSelect, (midi, device) => {
  console.log('Device connected');
});
manager.connectChannelSelection(channelSelect);
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

### populateDeviceList

Populate a device select element with available MIDI output devices. Automatically
handles maintaining selection when the current device remains connected, and clears
selection when the current device is disconnected. Updates status message accordingly.

#### Parameters

*   `selectElement` **[HTMLSelectElement][306]** The select element to populate with devices
*   `onChange` **[Function][301]?** Optional callback invoked after populating the list

#### Examples

```javascript
// Basic population
const deviceSelect = document.getElementById('device-select');
manager.populateDeviceList(deviceSelect);
```

```javascript
// With refresh callback
manager.populateDeviceList(deviceSelect, () => {
  console.log('Device list updated');
});
```

```javascript
// Combined with device listeners for automatic refresh
manager.setupDeviceListeners(() => {
  manager.populateDeviceList(deviceSelect);
});
manager.populateDeviceList(deviceSelect); // Initial population
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

## EventEmitter

Lightweight browser-compatible event emitter.
Provides publish/subscribe functionality for MIDI events
without external dependencies. Implements standard event
emitter pattern: register listeners with on(), emit events
with emit(), remove listeners with off(). Listener cleanup
is automatic via returned unsubscribe functions.

### on

Register an event listener

#### Parameters

*   `event` **[string][298]** Event name
*   `handler` **[Function][301]** Event handler function

Returns **[Function][301]** Unsubscribe function

### once

Register a one-time event listener

#### Parameters

*   `event` **[string][298]** Event name
*   `handler` **[Function][301]** Event handler function

### off

Remove an event listener

#### Parameters

*   `event` **[string][298]** Event name
*   `handler` **[Function][301]** Event handler function

### emit

Emit an event

#### Parameters

*   `event` **[string][298]** Event name
*   `data` **any** Event data

### removeAllListeners

Remove all event listeners

#### Parameters

*   `event` **[string][298]?** Optional event name to clear specific event

## DX7ParseError

*   **See**: [https://github.com/asb2m10/dexed][307]

DX7 Voice (patch) parser and manipulator for Yamaha DX7 SYX files

Handles both the 128-byte packed format (DX7 internal format) and
169-byte unpacked format (full parameter set with all operators).

Features:

*   Parse native DX7 voices from SYX banks or single voice files
*   Convert between packed (128-byte) and unpacked (169-byte) formats
*   Import/export JSON representation with human-readable parameters
*   Translate special DX7 characters for compatibility
*   Calculate checksums for SysEx validation
*   Support for algorithm configurations (1-32)
*   Per-operator parameter access (EG, scaling, frequency, output)
*   LFO and pitch envelope parameters
*   Global voice parameters (algorithm, feedback, transpose, etc.)

Based on Dexed implementation by Pascal Gauthier

## DX7ValidationError

**Extends DX7Error**

Error thrown when DX7 parameter validation fails

### Parameters

*   `message` &#x20;
*   `validationType` &#x20;
*   `value` &#x20;

## CONNECTION\_EVENTS

Connection event constants

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `DEVICE_CHANGE` **[string][298]** Emitted when any MIDI device state changes (connect/disconnect)
*   `IN_DEV_CONNECTED` **[string][298]** Emitted when an input device is connected
*   `IN_DEV_DISCONNECTED` **[string][298]** Emitted when an input device is disconnected
*   `OUT_DEV_CONNECTED` **[string][298]** Emitted when an output device is connected
*   `OUT_DEV_DISCONNECTED` **[string][298]** Emitted when an output device is disconnected

### Examples

```javascript
connection.on(CONNECTION_EVENTS.DEVICE_CHANGE, ({ port, state, type, device }) => {
  console.log(`${device.name} ${state}`);
});

connection.on(CONNECTION_EVENTS.OUT_DEV_CONNECTED, ({ device }) => {
  console.log(`Output connected: ${device.name}`);
});
```

## MIDIConnection

**Extends EventEmitter**

Low-level Web MIDI API connection handler. Manages:

*   MIDI device access/request
*   Device enumeration (inputs/outputs)
*   Device connection/disconnection
*   Hotplug detection and events
*   Raw MIDI message sending/receiving
*   SysEx message handling
*   Connection state tracking

NOTE: Typically used internally by MIDIController. Most applications
should use MIDIController instead for higher-level APIs.

### Parameters

*   `options` **[Object][297]**  (optional, default `{}`)

### Examples

```javascript
// Basic usage
const connection = new MIDIConnection({ sysex: true });
await connection.requestAccess();
await connection.connect('My MIDI Device');
connection.send([0x90, 60, 100]); // Note on
```

```javascript
// Listening for device changes
connection.on(CONNECTION_EVENTS.DEVICE_CHANGE, ({ device, state }) => {
  console.log(`${device.name} is now ${state}`);
});
```

### requestAccess

Request MIDI access from the browser. Sets up hotplug detection and
emits events when devices connect/disconnect.

#### Examples

```javascript
// Request basic MIDI access
await connection.requestAccess();
```

```javascript
// Request with SysEx support
const connection = new MIDIConnection({ sysex: true });
await connection.requestAccess();
```

*   Throws **[MIDIAccessError][147]** If MIDI is not supported or access is denied

Returns **[Promise][302]\<void>**&#x20;

### connect

Connect to a MIDI output device. Can connect by index, name, or ID.

#### Parameters

*   `device` **([string][298] | [number][299])?** Device name, ID, or index (defaults to first available)

#### Examples

```javascript
// Connect to first available device
await connection.connect();
```

```javascript
// Connect by index
await connection.connect(0);
```

```javascript
// Connect by name
await connection.connect('My MIDI Keyboard');
```

```javascript
// Connect by device ID
await connection.connect('input-12345');
```

*   Throws **[MIDIConnectionError][149]** If MIDI access not initialized
*   Throws **[MIDIDeviceError][151]** If device not found or index out of range

Returns **[Promise][302]\<void>**&#x20;

### connectInput

Connect to a MIDI input device for receiving messages

#### Parameters

*   `device` **([string][298] | [number][299])?** Device name, ID, or index (defaults to first available)
*   `onMessage` **[Function][301]** Callback for incoming MIDI messages

<!---->

*   Throws **[MIDIConnectionError][149]** If MIDI access not initialized
*   Throws **[MIDIValidationError][153]** If onMessage is not a function
*   Throws **[MIDIDeviceError][151]** If device not found or index out of range

Returns **[Promise][302]\<void>**&#x20;

### disconnectOutput

Disconnect from current output

### disconnectInput

Disconnect from current input

### disconnect

Disconnect from both output and input

### isConnected

Check if currently connected to an output

Returns **[boolean][300]**&#x20;

### getCurrentOutput

Get current output device info

Returns **([Object][297] | null)**&#x20;

### getCurrentInput

Get current input device info

Returns **([Object][297] | null)**&#x20;

### getOutputs

Get all available MIDI outputs

Returns **[Array][304]<{id: [string][298], name: [string][298], manufacturer: [string][298]}>**&#x20;

### getInputs

Get all available MIDI inputs

Returns **[Array][304]<{id: [string][298], name: [string][298], manufacturer: [string][298]}>**&#x20;

### send

Send a MIDI message to the connected output. Automatically converts
Arrays to Uint8Array for Web MIDI API compatibility.

#### Parameters

*   `message` **([Uint8Array][308] | [Array][304]<[number][299]>)** MIDI message bytes (e.g., \[0x90, 60, 100])
*   `timestamp` **[number][299]** Optional timestamp for scheduled sending (optional, default `performance.now()`)

#### Examples

```javascript
// Send a note on message (channel 1, note C4, velocity 100)
connection.send([0x90, 60, 100]);
```

```javascript
// Send a note off message
connection.send([0x80, 60, 0]);
```

```javascript
// Send a control change
connection.send([0xB0, 7, 64]); // Volume to 64
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

### sendSysEx

Send a System Exclusive (SysEx) message. Requires sysex: true in constructor options.

#### Parameters

*   `data` **[Array][304]<[number][299]>** SysEx data bytes (without F0/F7 wrapper)
*   `includeWrapper` **[boolean][300]** If true, wraps data with F0/F7 bytes (optional, default `false`)

#### Examples

```javascript
// Send a basic SysEx message (will be wrapped with F0/F7)
connection.sendSysEx([0x41, 0x10, 0x42, 0x12, 0x40, 0x00, 0x7F]);
```

```javascript
// Send pre-wrapped SysEx message
connection.sendSysEx([0xF0, 0x41, 0x10, 0x42, 0xF7], false);
```

Returns **void**&#x20;

## DX7Bank

Represents a DX7 bank (collection of 32 voices) loaded from a SYX file.
DX7 banks contain 32 voices in a packed 128-byte format with a 6-byte SysEx header,
4096 bytes of voice data, 1 byte checksum, and 0xF7 trailer. Provides methods for
loading from files, converting to/from SysEx format, and manipulating voices.

### Parameters

*   `data` **([Array][304]<[number][299]> | [ArrayBuffer][309] | [Uint8Array][308])?** Bank SYX data (4104 bytes with SysEx wrapper or 4096 bytes raw)
*   `name` **[string][298]** Optional bank name (e.g., filename without extension) (optional, default `""`)

### Examples

```javascript
// Load from file
const fileInput = document.getElementById('file-input');
fileInput.addEventListener('change', async (e) => {
  const file = e.target.files[0];
  const bank = await DX7Bank.fromFile(file);
  console.log(bank.getVoiceNames());
});
```

```javascript
// Create from SysEx data
const syxData = new Uint8Array([0xF0, 0x43, 0x00, 0x09, 0x20, 0x00, 0xF7]);
const bank = DX7Bank.fromSysEx(syxData, 'My Bank');
```

```javascript
// Manipulate voices
const bank = new DX7Bank();
const voice = DX7Voice.fromName('BASS 1');
bank.replaceVoice(0, voice); // Replace first voice
console.log(bank.getVoice(0).name); // 'BASS 1'
```

```javascript
// Export to SysEx
const bank = await DX7Bank.fromFile(file);
const syxData = bank.toSysEx();
download(syxData, 'my-bank.syx');
```

```javascript
// Convert to JSON for storage
const bank = await DX7Bank.fromFile(file);
const json = bank.toJSON();
localStorage.setItem('dx7-bank', JSON.stringify(json));
```

### replaceVoice

Replace a voice at the specified index (0-31). Validates the index and creates a copy
of the voice data to ensure the bank maintains its own independent copy.

#### Parameters

*   `index` **[number][299]** Voice index (0-31)
*   `voice` **[DX7Voice][219]** Voice to insert

#### Examples

```javascript
// Replace first voice with a custom voice
const bank = await DX7Bank.fromFile(file);
const customVoice = DX7Voice.fromName('LEAD 1');
bank.replaceVoice(0, customVoice);
console.log(bank.getVoice(0).name); // 'LEAD 1'
```

```javascript
// Swap voices between banks
const bank1 = await DX7Bank.fromFile(file1);
const bank2 = await DX7Bank.fromFile(file2);
const voiceFromBank2 = bank2.getVoice(5);
bank1.replaceVoice(0, voiceFromBank2); // Copy voice from bank2 to bank1
```

*   Throws **[DX7ValidationError][160]** If index is out of range (0-31)

Returns **void**&#x20;

### addVoice

Add a voice to the first empty slot

#### Parameters

*   `voice` **[DX7Voice][219]** Voice to add

Returns **[number][299]** Index where voice was added, or -1 if bank is full

### getVoices

Get all voices in the bank

Returns **[Array][304]<[DX7Voice][219]>**&#x20;

### getVoice

Get a specific voice by index

#### Parameters

*   `index` **[number][299]** Voice index (0-31)

Returns **([DX7Voice][219] | null)**&#x20;

### getVoiceNames

Get all voice names

Returns **[Array][304]<[string][298]>**&#x20;

### findVoiceByName

Find a voice by name (case-insensitive, partial match)

#### Parameters

*   `name` **[string][298]** Voice name to search for

Returns **([DX7Voice][219] | null)**&#x20;

Export bank to SysEx format

Returns **[Uint8Array][308]** Full SysEx data (4104 bytes)

Returns **[object][297]** Bank data in JSON format

### fromFile

Load a DX7 bank from a file

#### Parameters

*   `file` **(File | [Blob][310])** SYX file to load

<!---->

*   Throws **[DX7ParseError][157]** If file is a single voice file
*   Throws **[DX7ValidationError][160]** If data is not valid DX7 SYX format
*   Throws **[Error][311]** If file cannot be read (FileReader error)

Returns **[Promise][302]<[DX7Bank][189]>**&#x20;

### fromSysEx

Create a DX7Bank from SysEx data

#### Parameters

*   `name` **[string][298]** Optional bank name (optional, default `""`)

<!---->

*   Throws **[DX7ParseError][157]** If SysEx header is invalid

Returns **[DX7Bank][189]**&#x20;

Create a DX7Bank from a JSON object

Returns **[DX7Bank][189]**&#x20;

## DX7OperatorJSON

JSON representation of a DX7 operator (human-readable)

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `id` **[number][299]** Operator number (1-6)
*   `osc` **[Object][297]** Oscillator parameters (frequency, detune)
*   `eg` **[Object][297]** Envelope generator (rates and levels)
*   `key` **[Object][297]** Key scaling parameters (break point, velocity)
*   `output` **[Object][297]** Output parameters (level, amp mod sensitivity)
*   `scale` **[Object][297]** Keyboard scaling (left/right curves and depths)

## DX7VoiceJSON

JSON representation of a DX7 voice (patch)

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `name` **[string][298]** Voice/patch name (max 10 characters)
*   `operators` **[Array][304]<[DX7OperatorJSON][211]>** Array of 6 operators
*   `pitchEG` **[Object][297]** Pitch envelope generator (rates and levels)
*   `lfo` **[Object][297]** Low frequency oscillator parameters
*   `global` **[Object][297]** Global voice parameters (algorithm, feedback, transpose, etc.)

## DX7VoiceIndexJSON

JSON representation of a DX7 voice with bank index

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `index` **[number][299]** Voice index in bank (1-32)
*   `name` **[string][298]** Voice/patch name
*   `operators` **[Array][304]<[DX7OperatorJSON][211]>** Array of 6 operators
*   `pitchEG` **[Object][297]** Pitch envelope parameters
*   `lfo` **[Object][297]** LFO parameters
*   `global` **[Object][297]** Global voice parameters

## DX7BankJSON

Type: [Object][297]

### Properties

*   `version` **[string][298]** Version string (e.g., "1.0")
*   `name` **[string][298]** Bank name (e.g., filename)
*   `voices` **[Array][304]<[DX7VoiceIndexJSON][215]>** Array of 32 voices

## DX7Voice

DX7 Voice (patch) structure
Represents a single DX7 voice/patch with 6 operators, algorithm selection,
LFO, pitch envelope, and global parameters.

Supports two formats:

*   **Packed format (128 bytes)**: DX7 internal format with bit-packed parameters
*   **Unpacked format (169 bytes)**: Decompressed format with all parameters expanded

Each voice contains:

*   6 FM operators with individual EGs, frequency, output level, and scaling
*   Algorithm selection (1-32) for operator routing
*   Feedback loop (0-7) for algorithm feedback
*   LFO parameters (speed, delay, depth, wave shape)
*   Pitch envelope generator (4 rates, 4 levels)
*   Global parameters (transpose, pitch mod sensitivity, etc.)
*   10-character voice name

### Parameters

*   `data` **([Array][304]<[number][299]> | [Uint8Array][308])** 128 bytes of voice data
*   `index` **[number][299]** Voice index (0-31) (optional, default `0`)

### Examples

```javascript
// Create a voice from packed DX7 bank data
const bankData = new Uint8Array(...); // 4096 bytes for 32 voices
const voiceIndex = 5; // 6th voice in bank
const voiceData = bankData.subarray(voiceIndex * 128, (voiceIndex + 1) * 128);
const voice = new DX7Voice(voiceData, voiceIndex);
console.log(voice.name); // e.g., "BASS 1"
```

```javascript
// Load a voice from a single-voice SYX file
const file = document.getElementById('voice-file').files[0];
const voice = await DX7Voice.fromFile(file);
console.log(voice.toJSON());
```

```javascript
// Create from JSON and export to SysEx
const json = loadVoiceData();
const voice = DX7Voice.fromJSON(json);
const syxData = voice.toSysEx(); // For single voice synths like Volca FM
const packed = voice.data; // 128 bytes for DX7 bank
```

```javascript
// Modify operator parameters
const voice = await DX7Voice.fromFile(file);
const unpacked = voice.unpack();
unpacked[DX7Voice.UNPACKED_OP_OUTPUT_LEVEL] = 80; // Change OP1 output level
unpacked[DX7Voice.UNPACKED_ALGORITHM] = 5; // Change to algorithm 6
const modifiedVoice = DX7Voice.fromUnpacked(unpacked);
```

### getParameter

Get a raw parameter value from the packed data

#### Parameters

*   `offset` **[number][299]** Byte offset in the voice data (0-127)

<!---->

*   Throws **[DX7ValidationError][160]** If offset is out of range

Returns **[number][299]** Parameter value (0-127)

### getUnpackedParameter

Get a parameter value from the unpacked 169-byte format

#### Parameters

*   `offset` **[number][299]** Byte offset in the unpacked data (0-168)

<!---->

*   Throws **[DX7ValidationError][160]** If offset is out of range

Returns **[number][299]** Parameter value (0-127)

### setParameter

Set a raw parameter value in the packed data

#### Parameters

*   `offset` **[number][299]** Byte offset in the voice data
*   `value` **[number][299]** Parameter value (0-127)

### unpack

Unpack the voice data to 169-byte unpacked format
This converts the packed 128-byte format to the full DX7 parameter set

Returns **[Uint8Array][308]** 169 bytes of unpacked voice data (138 operator + 8 pitch EG + 13 global + 10 name = 169 bytes)

### toSysEx

Export voice to DX7 single voice SysEx format (VCED format)
This is useful for synths that only support single voice dumps (e.g., KORG Volca FM)
Converts from 169-byte unpacked format to 155-byte VCED format

Returns **[Uint8Array][308]** Single voice SysEx data (163 bytes)

### toJSON

Convert voice to JSON format

Returns **[object][297]** Voice data in JSON format

### pack

Pack 169-byte unpacked data to 128-byte format

#### Parameters

*   `unpacked` **([Array][304]<[number][299]> | [Uint8Array][308])** 169 bytes of unpacked data (159 parameters + 10 name bytes)

Returns **[Uint8Array][308]** 128 bytes of packed data

### createDefault

Create a default/empty voice

#### Parameters

*   `index` **[number][299]** Voice index (optional, default `0`)

Returns **[DX7Voice][219]**&#x20;

### fromUnpacked

Create a voice from unpacked 169-byte data

#### Parameters

*   `unpacked` **([Array][304]<[number][299]> | [Uint8Array][308])** 169 bytes of unpacked data (159 parameters + 10 name bytes)
*   `index` **[number][299]** Voice index (optional, default `0`)

Returns **[DX7Voice][219]**&#x20;

### fromFile

Load a DX7 voice from a single voice SYX file

#### Parameters

*   `file` **(File | [Blob][310])** SYX file (single voice in VCED format)

<!---->

*   Throws **[DX7ParseError][157]** If file has invalid VCED header
*   Throws **[Error][311]** If file cannot be read (FileReader error)

Returns **[Promise][302]<[DX7Voice][219]>**&#x20;

### fromSysEx

Create a DX7Voice from SysEx data

#### Parameters

*   `data` **([Array][304]<[number][299]> | [ArrayBuffer][309] | [Uint8Array][308])** Voice data (128 bytes of packed voice data) or VCED SysEx data (163 bytes with header/footer)
*   `index` **[number][299]** Voice index (optional, defaults to 0) (optional, default `0`)

<!---->

*   Throws **[DX7ParseError][157]** If VCED header is invalid
*   Throws **[DX7ValidationError][160]** If data length is invalid

Returns **[DX7Voice][219]**&#x20;

### fromJSON

Create a DX7Voice from a JSON object

#### Parameters

*   `json` **[DX7VoiceJSON][213]** JSON representation of a DX7 voice
*   `index` **[number][299]** Voice index (optional, defaults to 0) (optional, default `0`)

<!---->

*   Throws **[DX7ValidationError][160]** If JSON structure is invalid

Returns **[DX7Voice][219]**&#x20;
